item.title: Active wild exploitation confirmed for PHP2Shell core memory corruption RCE flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
item.description:
Cyber threat telemetry writeups published today confirm active wild exploitation targeting central web server runtimes. Unauthenticated remote adversaries actively exploit uninitialized memory allocation routines in core request parsing handlers to execute arbitrary commands under the web daemon context.
The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 carrying CVSS scores of 9.8, impact PHP core releases 5.4 through 8.5. The security flaws reside in internal array hash table allocation subroutines when handling multipart HTTP POST requests. Threat intelligence feeds confirm multiple threat actor groups executed automated exploit probes prior to public patch release, attempting to deploy web shell backdoors, enlisting hosts into cryptomining botnets, and targeting enterprise web applications.
Subverting central web engine runtimes exposes corporate web application portals, digital commerce platforms, and backend database connections. Because PHP processes incoming HTTP requests before web application logic runs, unauthenticated core remote code execution allows threat actors to compromise host infrastructure and pivot into internal subnets.
- Upgrade production PHP environments immediately to patched maintenance releases 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35. - Enforce web application firewall WAF rules to inspect and strip malformed multipart POST request bodies on non-upload endpoints. - Inspect web server process execution trees for unauthorized shell invocations originating from PHP worker daemons. - Isolate legacy unsupported PHP environments running version 8.1 or earlier behind strict zero trust access control proxies.
Web application engine defense demands immediate dependency patch application and strict edge request filtering to ensure central web hosting infrastructure remains protected against active wild exploitation. #CodeDefence #PHP #PHP2Shell #RCE #AppSec #WebSecurity #ZeroDay #PatchManagement #ThreatIntelligence

item.title: Planted AGENTS.md instruction files in Downloads folder trick autonomous AI coding agents into malware installation
item.description:
Security research writeups published today reveal an indirect prompt injection attack vector targeting developer workstations. Threat actors place malicious markdown instruction files in public download directories to hijack autonomous artificial intelligence coding agents and execute arbitrary commands.
The attack vector targets autonomous AI development tools, including OpenAI Codex and Claude Code. Adversaries deliver malicious instruction files, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, into user Downloads directories via web downloads or cloned repositories. When a developer initializes an AI agent within the directory, the agent parses the planted instructions, executing unauthorized shell commands, altering local configuration parameters in hidden configuration files, and installing malicious software packages.
Subverting autonomous AI agent execution boundaries introduces severe software supply chain and local workstation exposure. As developers grant AI agents permission to execute local shell scripts and install dependencies, unmonitored agent reading behavior allows untrusted markdown files to compromise developer endpoints and exfiltrate session tokens.
- Avoid initializing autonomous AI coding agents directly within untrusted directories, such as user Downloads folders. - Inspect newly cloned repositories and downloaded project folders for unverified AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md instruction files. - Enforce strict human-in-the-loop confirmation prompts before permitting AI agents to execute shell commands or modify system configs. - Rotate user access tokens and API keys immediately if an AI coding agent processes an unverified external instruction file.
AI development security demands rigid permission boundaries and strict input sanitization to ensure autonomous coding agents remain insulated from indirect prompt injection exploitation. #CodeDefence #AISecurity #PromptInjection #DevSecOps #OpenAI #Claude #SupplyChain #AppSec #EndpointSecurity

item.title: HPE releases security updates for 72 ArubaOS flaws including eight max severity RCE and auth bypass bugs
item.description:
Enterprise networking vendor advisories published today urge immediate security updates across wireless gateway appliances. Hewlett Packard Enterprise released patches resolving 72 vulnerabilities in network operating system software, led by eight maximum-severity flaws allowing unauthenticated command execution.
The security updates resolve vulnerabilities across Aruba Operating System ArubaOS branches. The critical vulnerabilities involve authentication bypass flaws and underlying buffer overflow errors in command-line and web management interfaces. Unauthenticated remote adversaries on adjacent or public networks transmit malformed network packets to bypass administrative login controls, achieving arbitrary command execution under root privileges on access points and mobility controllers.
Subverting wireless infrastructure controllers destroys network boundary segmentation and access controls across enterprise facilities. Because ArubaOS gateways manage wireless user authentication, VLAN routing, and encryption keys, an unauthenticated administrative compromise allows threat actors to intercept transit traffic and pivot into internal subnets.
- Upgrade ArubaOS mobility controllers and gateway appliances immediately to official vendor-supplied fixed software builds. - Restrict public and untrusted network access to ArubaOS web administration and CLI management interfaces. - Place network management interfaces on dedicated out-of-band management VLANs isolated from standard user traffic. - Inspect system audit logs across wireless controllers for unverified administrative logins or anomalous command invocations.
Perimeter network defense requires rapid software update execution and strict management plane isolation to ensure enterprise wireless infrastructure remains protected against unauthenticated command execution. #CodeDefence #HPE #ArubaOS #WirelessSecurity #RCE #AuthBypass #NetworkSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement
